explanation.heading: LESSON OBJECTIVE
explanation.text: Solve combined-event probability questions involving AND, OR, independent or dependent events, complements, and conditional probability. Identify the event relationship before calculating.

explanation.heading: WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW
explanation.text: An event is a set of outcomes. AND requires both conditions; OR requires at least one. The first draw changes the second probability if objects are not replaced.

explanation.heading: KEY DEFINITIONS
explanation.text: Independent: one event does not change the other's probability. Dependent: one event changes another's probability. Mutually exclusive: events cannot happen together. Conditional P(B|A): probability of B given A. Complement: event does not occur.

explanation.heading: CORE RULE
explanation.text: P(A and B)=P(A)P(B|A); independent events use P(A)P(B). P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A and B). P(at least one)=1−P(none).

explanation.heading: HOW IT WORKS
explanation.text: 1. Define A and B. 2. Decide AND, OR, complement, or conditional. 3. Check replacement/independence. 4. Count or use a tree. 5. Check the answer is between 0 and 1.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — INDEPENDENT
explanation.text: Flip a coin and roll a die. P(head AND 4)=(1/2)(1/6)=1/12. The trials do not influence one another.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — DEPENDENT
explanation.text: With 4 red and 3 blue counters, P(two red without replacement)=(4/7)(3/6)=2/7. Both counts change after a red is removed.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — OVERLAPPING OR
explanation.text: For a die, even outcomes {2,4,6} and outcomes >4 {5,6} overlap at 6. Union probability =3/6+2/6−1/6=2/3.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — COMPLEMENT
explanation.text: For two dice, P(at least one six)=1−P(no six on both)=1−(5/6)²=11/36.

explanation.heading: WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — TOTAL PROBABILITY
explanation.text: Rain occurs on 40% of days. Delay rates are 60% in rain and 10% in dry weather. P(delay)=(0.4)(0.6)+(0.6)(0.1)=0.30.

explanation.heading: PROBABILITY TREE
explanation.text: Draw branches for each possible first outcome; branch probabilities add to 1. Multiply along a path for AND, and add distinct successful paths. Without replacement, recompute second-stage probabilities.

explanation.heading: COMMON MISTAKES
explanation.text: Do not add for AND, forget to subtract overlap for OR, or treat without-replacement draws as independent. 'At least one' includes all positive counts. A conditional question restricts the denominator.

explanation.heading: EXAM STRATEGY
explanation.text: Translate words into A∩B, A∪B, or P(B|A). Use the complement for 'at least one'; a Venn diagram for overlap; and a tree for multi-stage trials.

explanation.heading: QUICK CHECK
explanation.text: Two heads in two fair flips? 1/4. If P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.5, overlap=0.2, then P(A or B)=0.9. Two reds from 3 red and 2 blue without replacement? 3/10.

explanation.heading: LESSON RECAP
explanation.text: AND: multiply using conditional second probability. OR: add and subtract overlap. At least one: subtract none from 1. Conditional: restrict the sample space.

explanation.heading: NEXT STEP
explanation.text: Complete 18 practice questions, compare the 18 worked solutions, then submit the five-question test. Review either full-lesson language route.

practice.question: Flip a fair coin and roll a fair die. P(head AND 4)?
Toss two fair coins. P(two tails)?
practice.solution: TT is one of four equally likely ordered outcomes.

practice.question: Roll one fair die. P(even OR greater than 4)?
Bag: 3 red, 2 blue. Replace after first draw. P(red then red)?
practice.solution: Replacement keeps 3/5 red on both draws: 9/25.

practice.question: Bag: 5 green, 3 yellow. No replacement. P(green then yellow)?
practice.solution: Multiply 5/8 by 3/7 after removing a green.

practice.question: Ten counters: 4 red, 6 blue. No replacement. P(two red)?
Two fair dice. P(sum of 7)?
practice.solution: Six ordered pairs sum to 7 among 36 possible pairs.

practice.question: Two fair dice. P(at least one six)?
One card from a standard deck. P(heart OR king)?
Class of 10: 6 in choir, 5 in band, 3 in both. P(choir OR band)?
Box: 4 defective, 16 good. Draw two without replacement. P(at least one defective)?
Eight finalists: five girls and three boys. Choose two without replacement. P(two girls)?
Independent A and B: P(A)=0.30, P(B)=0.40. Find P(A OR B).
Rain on 40% of days; delays on 60% of rainy and 10% of dry days. P(delay)?
Bag: 2 red, 3 blue. Draw two without replacement. P(one of each, any order)?
Flip a fair coin three times. P(exactly two heads)?
practice.solution: HHT, HTH, THH: three of eight equally likely outcomes.

practice.question: Machine A supplies 60% of products with 2% defective; B supplies 40% with 5% defective. P(defective)?
60 students: 35 take math, 30 art, 15 both. Given math, P(art)?
practice.solution: Condition restricts denominator to 35 math students: 15/35=3/7.

test.question: Toss three fair coins. P(all tails)?
Roll a fair die. P(even OR multiple of 3)?
Bag: 7 red, 3 green. Draw two without replacement. P(both green)?
40 customers: 24 buy tea, 19 coffee, 8 both. P(neither)?
60% of flights depart in morning (10% delayed); 40% later (25% delayed). P(delayed)?

english.title: What are combined events?
english.narration: Learn to tell AND from OR and conditional probability.

english.title: Outcome sets
english.narration: Define the sample space and count equally likely outcomes.

english.title: AND rule
english.narration: For both events, multiply first probability by the conditional second probability.

english.title: Independent events
english.narration: Coin and die: head and four has probability one twelfth.

english.title: Dependent events
english.narration: Without replacement, the second draw uses updated counts.

english.title: Replacement
english.narration: With replacement, original proportions remain unchanged.

english.title: OR rule
english.narration: Add event probabilities, subtract their shared outcomes.

english.title: Overlap
english.narration: Heart or king counts the king of hearts only once.

english.title: Complement
english.narration: At least one equals one minus none.

english.title: Conditional probability
english.narration: Given math, divide by the math group size.

english.title: Total probability
english.narration: Multiply along branches, add disjoint successful branches.

english.title: SAT strategy
english.narration: Choose the event rule first, then compute and check.
